name: google-finance-quote
title: Apple Inc (AAPL) Stock Price & News - Google Finance

knownGaps.why: Genuine limitation. A quote page carries an $0.11 dividend beside a $147 billion market cap — twelve orders of magnitude. The median grid (share prices, three decimals) fits neither end.

Two separate things are red here and only one of them is a limitation.
(1) OPEN PRODUCT QUESTION: $109.42 billion renders as 140,282,051 ZEC. That is nearly seven times the entire 21 million ZEC supply, so it is a number no reader can use as a unit of account even though it is arithmetically right. Undecided; recorded, not fixed.
(2) DEFECT, not a limitation: "$108.959 billion" renders as 139,691,025,641 ZEC and "$109.417 billion" as 140,278,205,128 ZEC — both exactly 1000x too high. parseNumber in src/lib/detection/parser.ts takes the dot in "108.959" for thousands grouping because its US-decimal escape only fires on a single-digit integer part (sepIndex <= 1). The multiplier word was already consumed by then, so the parser knows it is reading a mantissa and reads it wrong anyway. "$109.4 billion" on the same page comes out correct at 140,256,410 ZEC, which is the scale the other two should have landed on.
